start_here: Say to your AI: "Post 'Draft is ready for review.' with a link to my Spring menu draft (https://example.com/menu/spring) in Slack channel #general." It runs tool:post-to-slack.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it takes the things and note it is given and posts them once to the person's connected service.
instructions: 1. Connect Slack in your Trillion account (service_connection:slack); for a private channel invite the app to it first.
2. Pick the channel: its name like #general, or its id.
3. Say to your AI the start_here sentence; it calls tools:run for tool:post-to-slack with things, note and channel.
4. Read $.said, and look in the channel for the message with the linked attachment.

worked_examples.title: Post a picked note to a Slack channel
worked_examples.ask: Post a picked note to a Slack channel
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/send-to-a-place/tool-rows.json (the row's invoke body) and checked against tools/send-to-a-place/test/send-to-a-place-rows.test.mjs: the person has connected Slack (service_connection:slack). The body posts text "Draft is ready for review." in #general with an attachment titled "Spring menu draft" linking to https://example.com/menu/spring; Slack's own ok: false is treated as a refusal (answer_ok_field ok). I could not run it: it needs a live Slack bot token, so the answer is worked out from the row, and the exact "said" wording follows the webhook sibling's pattern "<host> answered <status>".
worked_examples.hands_back: {"status":200,"said":"slack.com answered 200","answer":"<Slack's reply as text, with ok true>"}. If Slack cannot find the channel it answers ok false and the reply is told in Slack's words (for example channel_not_found).
